title: Sixty drawings and one fox
scenario:
A bakery chain wants 60 menu drawings in its hand-drawn ink-and-wash look this year. Its mascot, a small fox, must look the same in every one. Your teammate wrote a style plan. You review it before anything is run or trained.

Use the exhibit. The chain, the files and the plan are made up for this case. The field names and limits are from the vendors' docs in October 2026.
exhibit:
ASSETS (made up)
  3 approved menu drawings (ink and wash, cream paper)
  8 photos of the fox mascot costume, all from the front
  The chain owns all of these files.

STYLE PLAN (draft, made up)
  Step 1  Recraft API: send the 3 drawings as style references
          AND the style_id saved last week, in the same request.
  Step 2  Ideogram: train a custom model on the 8 fox photos today.
  Step 3  FLUX.2 [klein] LoRA for the fox, captions like:
          "ink and wash drawing, soft wash, cream paper, fox"
  Step 4  When the fox model is done, click Publish so the
          franchise owners can find it.

questions.prompt: Recraft would reject Step 1 as written. Why?

options.text: A request can carry a style_id or style references, not both
options.explanation: Right. Recraft says the two are mutually exclusive: a request with both a style_id and style references is rejected.

options.text: A V4 style needs at least ten reference images before it runs
options.explanation: Recraft takes one to ten images, and says a single reference is enough to start.

options.text: Style references only work after a training job has finished
options.explanation: Recraft says no training or fine-tuning is required: attach the images and generate.

options.text: A saved style_id can be used once and then must be made again
options.explanation: Recraft calls a style a reusable blueprint, and returns a style_id so later requests can reuse it.

questions.prompt: Step 2 trains an Ideogram custom model on 8 fox photos. What is the problem?

options.text: Ideogram custom models only learn styles, never a subject
options.explanation: Ideogram asks for images "of the style or subject you want", so a subject is fine. The image count is the blocker here.

options.text: Ideogram needs 15 to 100 images; 8 photos are too few
options.explanation: Right. Ideogram lists 15 to 100 images of the style or subject you want.

options.text: Ideogram trains only on vector files, not on photos
options.explanation: Ideogram takes AVIF, HEIC, JPG, PNG or WebP files, or a ZIP.

options.text: Ideogram training is free, so the plan needs no budget
options.explanation: Ideogram shows a cost of 4,000 credits on the Start training button.

questions.prompt: Step 3: how should the fox LoRA captions change, by BFL's guide?

options.text: Add even more style words, so the style is stronger in the LoRA
options.explanation: BFL says to describe everything visible except the style or concept you want the model to learn.

options.text: Use one trigger word, and describe what is visible, not the style
options.explanation: Right. BFL says to include your trigger word consistently and describe everything visible except the style/concept you teach.

options.text: Leave every caption empty, so the model picks its own trigger
options.explanation: BFL asks for descriptive, detailed captions with a trigger word in each one.

options.text: Write a new trigger word in each caption, so each image differs
options.explanation: BFL says to include your trigger word consistently. One word switches the LoRA on.

questions.prompt: Step 4 publishes the fox model. What does that do on Ideogram?

options.text: Only the franchise owners on your team can see it after that
options.explanation: Sharing with a team is a separate option. Publish makes the model discoverable to anyone.

options.text: It turns the custom model into a style reference for Ideogram 4.5
options.explanation: Publish is about who can find the model. It does not change the model type.

options.text: Anyone can find and use it; share it with the team instead
options.explanation: Right. Ideogram says a published model is discoverable in the community gallery and anyone can use it. A team space can share it privately.

options.text: It moves the model to a newer base model than Ideogram 3.0
options.explanation: Ideogram says the base model reads Ideogram 3.0 and you can't change it.
